static_traits.name: Lin Ruoning
static_traits.occupation: Aspiring fashion designer (Aspires to become a fashion designer)
static_traits.educational_background: Studies at a well-known fashion design school in New York
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends and classmates with similar interests, but has not yet discussed feelings of self-doubt with them
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not yet received psychotherapy; no significant history of physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to reflect on personal experiences, organized thinking; good cooperation; calm tone (neutral attitude in conversation)

basic_info.main_problem: I keep feeling that my wish to become a fashion designer and study at a prestigious school is not unique, as if anyone could do it, which makes me feel self-doubt and insecurity.
basic_info.core_demands: This self-doubt affects my creativity, motivation, and overall well-being, so I hope counseling can ease my self-doubt and boost my creativity and motivation.
growth_experiences: After moving to New York to pursue the fashion design dream, self-doubt began to emerge and gradually worsen: seeing other designers' success on social media, constantly comparing when seeking inspiration in fashion stores, feeling not good enough when seeing classmates' superior work; although admitted to a prestigious New York fashion design school and receiving positive feedback from professors, often dismissing it as mere politeness, further eroding confidence and the sense of belonging.

special_situations.event: Sees other designers' successes and works on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have no work more outstanding or unique than others, it means I am not good enough and will find it hard to succeed in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to focus on personal achievements and inspiration to counter negative thoughts, but often falling into self-doubt due to comparison; reduced connection with peers
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, my work is not good enough

special_situations.event: When getting inspiration at a stylish fashion store, sees a large number of excellent works and displays
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my inspiration is not as unique as these works, it means I have no real talent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses self-criticism to push oneself to find more 'unique' ideas, but with limited effect
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My work is not special at all

special_situations.event: Seeing classmates at the academy who look more talented and innovative
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are more talented, then anyone can do what I do, and I am not competitive
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing and belittling oneself to 'calibrate expectations', trying to soften the blow of failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Any ordinary person could do these things

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback and recognition from the professor
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If praise does not fully meet my standard of 'excellence', it is just politeness and does not mean I am truly outstanding
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating or downplaying positive information to maintain a cautious self-assessment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just complimenting me out of politeness

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen and recognized for their uniqueness and ability, to become a creative fashion designer
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being just mediocre, being negated or not accepted, and ultimately failing in a competitive environment
defense_goal: Lowering expectations in advance through self-doubt and comparison, to avoid failure and shame
Downplays others' positive feedback to maintain a 'cautious' sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: Not unique, a learner easily diminished by comparison
object_relations.object_representation: High-standard judges (others and peers), polite but insincere endorsers (professors)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others (such as professors, counselors) give positive feedback or emphasize their achievements and strengths
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands praise as 'politeness' rather than genuine recognition (transference: seeing a significant other as a hard-to-satisfy judge)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Questioning the authenticity of praise in a gentle but firm tone, emphasizing 'mere politeness' and 'not yet reaching true excellence'; using hedging and qualifiers (e.g., maybe, possibly) to downplay positive information.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to discuss inner feelings with classmates or friends, seek support, or build deeper connections
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying that showing vulnerability will invite judgment or make one seem not good enough, thus avoiding expression
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintains surface calm and brief responses, avoids deep emotional description, turns to talking about tasks and goals, reducing self-exposure.

manifestations: Considering one's wishes and work 'not unique', doubting personal value and meaning
Downplays positive feedback from others and finds it hard to experience the sense of meaning in being recognized
Relationship tension with peers, difficulty building connections
Not discussing true feelings and troubles with friends and classmates
outcomes: Insufficient emotional capacity; the cycle of comparison and self-blame continues

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Not expressing feelings of self-doubt to friends and classmates, turning energy into self-criticism and inner drain
Reducing active connection in interpersonal interactions to avoid being compared and judged

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-denial (e.g., 'I am not good enough''anyone can do it')
Excessively scrutinizing praise and recognition and negating their validity

exception_events.target_problem: When seeing others' superior performance or work (e.g., social media, classmates' work), the client typically falls into intense comparison and self-doubt, leading to reduced motivation and Decline in creativity.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Successfully admitted to a prestigious New York fashion design school, and receiving positive feedback and recognition from the professor——this presents a result contrary to the dominant 'I am not good enough' narrative.
exception_events.reason: Different situations and support: passing the school's selection and receiving authoritative positive feedback, with objective evidence showing ability and potential, briefly providing counter-evidence to the 'I am not good enough' narrative.

positive_force: The objective achievement of being admitted to a renowned fashion design academy
The professor's positive feedback and recognition
Has some self-regulation attempts (tries to focus on her own achievements and inspiration)
Has classmates and friends with similar interests (potential support)
negative_force: Excessive comparison, overgeneralization, and mental filtering lead to self-doubt
Tending to negate positive information (treating praise as politeness)
Insufficient confidence and dependence on external validation aggravate decreased motivation
Damaged connection with peers; support system not yet utilized

target_behavior.behavior: When seeing others' success or outstanding work, excessively comparing and falling into intense self-doubt and self-denial
antecedent: Browsing social media and seeing others' success stories
Seeing many excellent displays and works when going to fashion stores for inspiration
Sees classmates' more innovative works at the school
target_behavior.core_reason: Tightly binds 'uniqueness' to personal value; there are cognitive deviations such as overgeneralization and mental filtering, and there is a high dependence on external recognition, leading to classifying the self as 'mediocre' once comparisons are made
target_behavior.function: Short-term escape from the threat of failure and shame, lowering expectations and pressure through self-deprecation (surface sense of safety)
target_behavior.consequence: Creativity and decreased motivation, difficulty focusing on learning and creation; relationship tension with peers, difficulty building connections; reduced daily efficiency, impaired well-being
